title: End drain cleanly when landed config needs a newer build
summary: When a landed job's athena.toml adds a key the running binary's schema rejects, the drain should keep the job recorded as landed and end the run with a "reinstall" note, not count a failure or stop on "repeated failure". Goal: a drain operator whose run lands a config-extending job sees a clean stop with reinstall guidance.

defaults_applied.how: The change and test are Rust.
New test plus cargo test, clippy, fmt criteria.
Fix is in how the drain classifies post-landing config parse errors, not a special case for one key.
Criteria check the recorded landed state and stop reason by running the test.
Behavior criteria name cargo test runs.
Reinstall note and CHANGELOG entry written for outside readers.
One focused change confined to drain and run code.
Enforced by a test rather than prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (Stop enum ~l.923-985, land() ~l.1617, item loop ~l.1700-1762, ItemEnd::Failed -> Stop::RepeatedFailure ~l.2308, RealSteps::caps/priority_caps calling JobConfig::at(head) ~l.3248/3332), crates/athena-core/src/capability.rs (JobConfig::at parses athena.toml with Config::parse, strict on unknown fields), crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs (configuration rule, unknown field), and the file list of crates/athena-core/src/run/. The exact place where the post-landing config parse error becomes a failed job was not pinned down; the producer must locate it by running the new test first.

The drain code lives in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (and its integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs); 'the drain code' in the request is read as that, plus crates/athena-core/src/run/ if the landing/record logic is there.

The new stop is a new Stop variant (or reuses Stop::Rebuilt-style handling) with a label and meaning that tells the user to reinstall; Stop::ALL and display/help text in crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs and main.rs stay consistent with it, which counts as drain code.
No new record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file/AnyRecord are unaffected; the job's recorded state stays landed.

Only a config parse failure at the landed commit is treated this way; a config that fails to parse on its own (not a newer-schema issue) cannot be told apart cheaply, so the producer may treat any parse error of the landed head config, when the landing itself succeeded, as this case, and says so in a code comment.
No change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows; the test uses a fixture config with a key the schema lacks.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (or the drain.rs unit tests) lands a job whose diff adds an unknown key to athena.toml; `cargo test -p athena-cli` passes, the test asserts the job's recorded outcome is landed (not failed), and the report's stop is not Stop::RepeatedFailure.
In that test the run's final report/output contains a note telling the user to reinstall, and the run ends cleanly (no failure counted for the item); checked by `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
A regression test shows a genuine failure (job that does not land twice) still ends with Stop::RepeatedFailure; `cargo test -p athena-cli` passes.
The change touches only files under crates/athena-core/src/run/, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, its stop display text, and their tests (git diff --stat), plus CHANGELOG.md.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing that a landed config the running build cannot parse ends the run cleanly with a reinstall note instead of a false repeated failure.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass (tested default).

The new stop reason (if added) has a label and meaning and is listed wherever stops are enumerated (Stop::ALL, help text in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs, display), verified by the existing test that every Stop has a meaning.

out_of_scope: Making the config parser tolerant of unknown keys
Automatically reinstalling or rebuilding the binary
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, or admission rules
Changes to the athena-gate crate or other crates beyond the drain and run code
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than reference: the failure site is not yet located, and the drain lives in athena-cli, which the request's path scope only loosely names.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time: a job that landed is wrongly recorded failed and halts the run with a false 'repeated failure'.
hard_reason: It changes the drain's stop and failure rules and the run pipeline's handling of a landed job, where a mistake could hide real failures.
